source_anchors.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 45 degrees and reaches a maximum height of 120 m. At its first impact with the ground it loses half its kinetic energy. Immediately after the bounce its velocity is at 30 degrees above the horizontal. Find the new maximum height.
conditions: First flight starts and ends at ground level.
Half the kinetic energy is lost at the first bounce.

source_anchors.stem: A projectile has ordinary range d when launched at speed v and angle theta under gravity g. At the highest point it enters a region where the effective downward acceleration is g/0.81. If its new total horizontal range is d'=n d, find n.
conditions: The acceleration changes only after the projectile reaches its apex.
Horizontal velocity is unchanged at the boundary.

source_anchors.stem: A 0.2 kg projectile is launched at 270 m/s at 60 degrees in a medium with linear drag F=-c v, where c=0.1 kg/s. It hits a vertical wall after 2 s. Taking e=2.7 for the exponential evaluation specified by the source, determine the horizontal distance to the wall.
conditions: Linear viscous drag acts opposite the instantaneous velocity.
source_anchors.answer: 170 m (within the official accepted interval 167–171 m).

source_anchors.stem: A projectile launched from O with speed v at angle theta passes through P, which is 5 m horizontally and 1 m vertically from O. Determine which source statements are correct about the required speed and whether the projectile reaches its maximum height before or after P for specified launch angles.
conditions: Uniform gravitational acceleration g acts downward.
Point P has coordinates (5 m,1 m) relative to launch point O.
options: (B) For theta=45°, maximum height is reached before P
(C) For theta=30°, maximum height is reached after P

source_anchors.stem: A projectile has coordinates x=24t and y=43.6t-4.9t^2, with x and y in metres and t in seconds. What angle does its velocity vector make with the horizontal at t=2 s?

authored_practice.stem: A particle has x(t)=10t and y(t)=18t-2t^2 in metres. Find the direction of its instantaneous velocity at t=2 s.
authored_practice.answer: The velocity components at 2 s are (10,10) m/s, so the direction is 45° above +x.

authored_practice.stem: A projectile launched at 45° reaches 80 m maximum height. On returning to the ground it retains 60% of its kinetic energy and rebounds at 30° above horizontal. Find its new maximum height.
authored_practice.answer: The new maximum height is 24 m.

authored_practice.stem: An ordinary projectile would have range R. At the apex it enters a region where downward gravity becomes 4g while horizontal velocity is unchanged. Express the new range as a fraction of R.
A projectile launched at 45° passes through P=(4 m,1 m). Find u²/g and decide whether the projectile is rising or falling at P.
authored_practice.answer: u²/g=16/3 m and the projectile is already descending at P.

authored_practice.stem: A projectile has horizontal launch component 120 m/s. In a medium with linear drag, m/c=2 s. Find its horizontal displacement after 2 s using e≈2.718.
A particle follows x=2t²+3t and y=12t-t². At t=1 s, decide the direction of motion. Neither velocity component is constant.
authored_practice.answer: At t=1 s, v_x=7 and v_y=10 m/s, so theta=tan^-1(10/7) above +x.

transfer.statement: Both component position laws now vary with time; the learner must independently choose differentiation as the representation before any angle calculation.

authored_practice.stem: A projectile returns to level ground with speed U. After impact it retains 36% of its kinetic energy, and its rebound velocity has vertical:horizontal component ratio 3:4. Find its next maximum height in terms of U and g.

transfer.statement: The rebound direction is supplied as a component ratio rather than an angle; the learner must still protect the energy-to-speed-squared decision before translating the new representation.

authored_practice.stem: A projectile reaches its apex at horizontal position L and height H with horizontal speed V. Immediately after the apex, downward gravity changes to g/4. Decide the additional horizontal distance before it reaches the launch level.

transfer.statement: The apex state is supplied directly and the target is only the second-stage displacement; the learner must decide to start from the boundary rather than reuse whole-flight symmetry.

authored_practice.stem: From the origin, can a finite-speed gravity-only projectile launched exactly along the straight line joining the origin to P=(5 m,1 m) pass through P? Justify without solving for a numerical speed.
authored_practice.answer: No finite speed can make it pass through P.

transfer.statement: Instead of solving for speed after point substitution, the learner must recognize a reachability boundary from the sign of the gravity term.

authored_practice.stem: A projectile's measured horizontal velocity halves every τ seconds in a medium. Decide whether x=v_x0 t is valid and write a horizontal displacement expression in terms of v_x0, τ and t consistent with linear drag.
authored_practice.answer: x=(v_x0 τ/ln2)[1-2^{-t/τ}], so x=v_x0 t is not valid except as a short-time/zero-drag limit.

transfer.statement: The drag parameter is given through a velocity half-life rather than c/m; the learner must recognize and translate the exponential representation before integrating.
